notes: Policy execution is not a decision: benefits, basic income, job-guarantee wages, upkeep and builds are paid as the player's levers say, so the government chooses only how to fund them, how to cut them pro rata and how its legitimacy moves (known-issues DP-10).
Tax collection and debt service are mechanics, not choices.
The estate pays the pilot in full each month, or what it holds up to the wage. That is accounting, not a choice, so it is not a registered decision (known-issues DP-11).

A flight adds its tonnes (estate.flight_tonnes) to emissions and the estate pays the carbon price (after lobbying) on them; the pilot's wage moves from the estate to the pilot's household. Both are accounting.

Nature is not an agent. It responds to cumulative emissions, the forest stock, commons use and the access rule, and to harvest and fire; only the enclosure of the commons is a registered decision. See the Forest and commons topic for growth and the sink.
Who encloses the commons is matched in the simulation (the richest capital-owning household), not decided here (known-issues DP-11).
Nothing is decided here: each capital-owning household's gift is a decision listed under Households. Here that money becomes pressure on policy levers, held back by union strength.
Nothing is decided here: the odds follow climate stress, dryness and fire station coverage, and the outcome is a random draw.

roles.label: Starting point
roles.text: No decision writes it: a state variable, a lever or a setting the chain starts from.

roles.label: In the middle
roles.text: A decision writes it and another decision reads it.

roles.label: End point
roles.text: Written by a decision, but no other decision reads it: an outcome.

roles.label: Decision
roles.text: A choice that reads some quantities and writes others.

aggregates.label: Town figure
aggregates.text: One number for the whole town.

aggregates.label: Total
aggregates.text: Added up over the active firms or over all households.

aggregates.label: Average
aggregates.text: The average over the active firms.

aggregates.label: Setting
aggregates.text: The setting of a policy lever now (the effective one where lobbying can change it).

aggregates.label: Yes or no
aggregates.text: Shown as 1 for yes and 0 for no.

unbound.label: Inside one agent
unbound.text: A working variable of a single firm, household or bank. The town has no one number for it.

unbound.label: Worked out each month
unbound.text: A rule computes it fresh every month and does not keep it, so there is no stored value to show.

unbound.label: Not shown yet
unbound.text: It exists in the simulation, but the game does not publish a town figure for it yet.

unbound.label: A fixed setting
unbound.text: A fixed setting of the model's rules rather than a number that moves.

unbound.label: Chance
unbound.text: A random draw, different every time, with no value to track.

quantities.label: Expected sales
quantities.summary: A smoothed average of past demand for what the firm makes.

quantities.label: Inventory
quantities.summary: Unsold stock the firm holds.

quantities.label: Inventory cover wanted
quantities.summary: How many months of sales the firm likes to hold as stock (services cannot be stored, so they hold none).

quantities.label: Workers
quantities.summary: The people the firm employs.

quantities.label: Skilled workers
quantities.summary: Workers whose skill is at or above the skilled threshold.

quantities.label: Effective labour per worker
quantities.summary: What an average worker contributes after skill and commute time.

quantities.label: Output from capital and technology
quantities.summary: What one unit of labour would make with the firm's capital and technology, before weather, resources and the transition take their share.

quantities.label: Weather and climate effect on output
quantities.summary: Climate damage, drought and smoke from nearby fires, which cut what a firm can make (climate damage and drought hit farms only).

quantities.label: Natural resources effect on output
quantities.summary: The health of the forest and commons a farm relies on, and the coordination cost of a community-managed commons.

quantities.label: Transition effect on output
quantities.summary: Output lost while the town changes its economic system.

quantities.label: Workers wanted
quantities.summary: The headcount that would produce the output the firm wants.

quantities.label: Vacancies
quantities.summary: Jobs the firm posts this month, skilled and general.

quantities.label: Months overstaffed
quantities.summary: How many months in a row the firm has had more workers than it wants.

quantities.label: Unemployment
quantities.summary: The town's smoothed unemployment rate, which firms watch when they set wages.

quantities.label: Base wage
quantities.summary: The firm's base monthly wage.

quantities.label: Minimum wage
quantities.summary: The legal wage floor (the player's lever).

quantities.label: Sector productivity growth
quantities.summary: How fast output per worker grows in the firm's sector; wages follow it so that wages and prices do not drift apart.

quantities.label: Price
quantities.summary: What the firm charges for one unit.

quantities.label: Markup
quantities.summary: The margin over unit cost the firm aims for. It is the firm's own state, set at the start and copied to a new firm, not a parameter.

quantities.label: Unit cost
quantities.summary: Wages plus carbon cost for each unit made.

quantities.label: Carbon footprint
quantities.summary: Direct emissions plus the emissions of the electricity the firm uses.

quantities.label: Carbon price firms plan with
quantities.summary: The carbon price in force after lobbying, pulled toward a price the player has announced but not yet started.

quantities.label: Revenue
quantities.summary: What the firm earned selling this month.

quantities.label: Emissions cap
quantities.summary: The cap in force after lobbying (0 means no cap).

quantities.label: Green subsidy
quantities.summary: The share of a green investment the treasury pays.

quantities.label: Treasury cash
quantities.summary: Cash the government holds; it limits the subsidies it can pay.

quantities.label: Cash
quantities.summary: Cash the firm holds when it decides.

quantities.label: Cash reserve
quantities.summary: Cash kept back for payroll and debt service.

quantities.label: Green technology
quantities.summary: How much of its emissions the firm has cut with clean technology.

quantities.label: Saving for green investment
quantities.summary: The firm wants a green step but cannot afford it yet, so it holds cash back.

quantities.label: Profit
quantities.summary: Profit after interest, carbon cost and tax this month.

quantities.label: Profit trend
quantities.summary: A smoothed average of past profit.

quantities.label: Capital
quantities.summary: The firm's capital stock after depreciation and this month's purchases.

quantities.label: Capital needed per unit sold
quantities.summary: How much capital the firm's technology needs for each unit of expected sales.

quantities.label: Loan rate
quantities.summary: The interest rate the bank charges the firm.

quantities.label: In distress
quantities.summary: The firm has been behind on payments or could not pay wages in full.

quantities.label: Required return above the loan rate
quantities.summary: How much more than the loan rate an investment must earn; set by the economic system.

quantities.label: Cash held for green investment
quantities.summary: The share of free cash held back while a green step is planned; set by the economic system.

quantities.label: Planned investment
quantities.summary: What the firm plans to spend on capital goods next month.

quantities.label: Loan request
quantities.summary: What the firm asks the bank to lend for its plan.

quantities.label: Wages paid
quantities.summary: What the firm paid its workers this month.

quantities.label: Debt service due
quantities.summary: Interest plus scheduled principal due this month.

quantities.label: Payout ratio
quantities.summary: The share of profit paid out; set by the economic system.

quantities.label: Dividends
quantities.summary: What the firm pays its owners this month.

quantities.label: Debt
quantities.summary: What the firm owes the bank.

quantities.label: Missed payments
quantities.summary: Interest, scheduled principal or wages went unpaid this month.

quantities.label: Months in distress
quantities.summary: How many months in a row the firm has missed payments.

quantities.label: Firm open
quantities.summary: Whether the firm keeps trading or defaults and closes.

quantities.label: Sector return
quantities.summary: The average return on capital in a sector that has room for another firm.

quantities.label: Cost of borrowing
quantities.summary: The base rate plus the bank's base spread.

quantities.label: Random draw
quantities.summary: A chance draw the simulation takes each month and hands to the decision.

quantities.label: New firm
quantities.summary: A household founds a firm in the dormant slot.

quantities.label: Savings
quantities.summary: The deposits a household holds.

quantities.label: Last month's disposable income
quantities.summary: Income after tax, rent and loan payments last month.

quantities.label: Net wealth
quantities.summary: Savings, homes and firm shares owned, less debt.

quantities.label: Food price
quantities.summary: The average price of food across the food firms.

quantities.label: Food need
quantities.summary: The food a household needs each month: a fixed amount per person.

quantities.label: Household size
quantities.summary: How many people live in the household.

quantities.label: Spending propensity
quantities.summary: The share of spare income a household of this class spends rather than saves.

quantities.label: Spending out of wealth
quantities.unit: share of net wealth per month
quantities.summary: The slice of net wealth the owner classes also spend each month (zero for other classes).

quantities.label: Spending budget
quantities.summary: The money a buyer brings to a market: households split theirs into food, goods and services; firms and the government buy in the same markets.

quantities.label: Demand
quantities.summary: What buyers wanted from the firm this month, in units, even if its stock ran out.

quantities.label: Units sold
quantities.summary: What the firm actually sold this month.

quantities.label: Capital income
quantities.summary: Dividends, rent and interest a household received last month.

quantities.label: Campaign spending cap
quantities.summary: The player-set limit on the share of income that may go to lobbying.

quantities.label: Lobbying spend
quantities.summary: What a capital-owning household gives to lobbying this month.

quantities.label: Bank equity
quantities.summary: The bank's own money: what its loans are worth less what it owes depositors.

quantities.label: Bank loans
quantities.summary: All the loans the bank has made.

quantities.label: Bank deposits
quantities.summary: What the bank owes its depositors.

quantities.label: Required capital ratio
quantities.summary: The player-set minimum of equity to loans.

quantities.label: Lending room
quantities.summary: How much more the bank may lend before it breaks the capital ratio.

quantities.label: Firm assets
quantities.summary: What a firm owns: capital at its price plus cash.

quantities.label: Loan approved
quantities.summary: What the bank agrees to lend the firm this month.

quantities.label: System credit spread
quantities.summary: Extra interest the economic system adds on top of the usual spread.

quantities.label: Bank dividend
quantities.summary: Equity above the required buffer that the bank pays to its owner.

quantities.label: Policy rate
quantities.summary: The base interest rate the player sets.

quantities.label: Bailout policy
quantities.summary: Whether the treasury recapitalises a failing bank.

quantities.label: Bank failed
quantities.summary: The bank is out of equity and has no bailout: depositors lose part of their savings.

quantities.label: Committed spending
quantities.summary: What the government owes this month: benefits, UBI, job-guarantee wages, upkeep and building.

quantities.label: Next month's purchases
quantities.summary: The goods the government plans to buy next month (the spending lever), held back in cash.

quantities.label: Taxes collected
quantities.summary: Taxes and carbon payments that came in this month.

quantities.label: Public debt
quantities.summary: What the government owes the bank.

quantities.label: Borrowing
quantities.summary: New loans the government takes from the bank this month.

quantities.label: Repayment
quantities.summary: Debt the government pays back this month.

quantities.label: Share of spending paid
quantities.summary: The share of each committed payment the treasury can actually fund (1 means all of it).

quantities.label: Legitimacy
quantities.summary: How far the town accepts the government's rule; it drifts with wellbeing, unemployment, inequality, debt, bailouts and system change.

quantities.label: Wellbeing
quantities.summary: The town's average wellbeing.

quantities.label: Inequality
quantities.summary: The Gini coefficient of household wealth.

quantities.label: Public debt against GDP
quantities.summary: Public debt divided by a year's GDP.

quantities.label: Bank bailed out
quantities.summary: Whether the treasury rescued the bank this month.

quantities.label: Resistance to system change
quantities.summary: The legitimacy lost each month while the town changes its economic system.

quantities.label: Pilot on the payroll
quantities.summary: Whether the jet's pilot works for the estate right now (true also when the town has no pilot to need).

quantities.label: Months of short pay
quantities.summary: How many months in a row the estate could not pay the pilot in full.

quantities.label: Pilot free to rehire
quantities.summary: The pilot has no other job and is not on the job guarantee.

quantities.label: Estate savings
quantities.summary: The deposits the estate household holds.

quantities.label: Jet flies
quantities.summary: Whether the jet flies this month.

quantities.label: Chance of enclosure
quantities.summary: The chance each month that a wealthy owner fences off an open commons; it depends on the economic system.

quantities.label: Commons open
quantities.summary: Whether anyone may use the commons (not enclosed and not community-managed).

quantities.label: Commons enclosed
quantities.summary: Whether an owner has fenced the commons off.

decisions.title: Hire
decisions.decides: How many workers to want and how many jobs to post (hiring up to a monthly cap)

rule.label: Size the workforce to expected sales and stock
rule.text: Needed output = expected sales x (1 + growth aspiration) + inventory adjust x (cover x expected sales - inventory). Workers wanted = labour that output needs, in people. It posts vacancies once the gap exceeds the hiring slack, and the skilled tier gets what it is short of.

decisions.title: Fire
decisions.decides: Whether to let people go: only after a sustained surplus of workers, the least skilled first

rule.label: Fire after months of surplus
rule.text: Each month the firm is overstaffed by at least the firing slack it counts one more month. After enough months in a row it lets go up to a monthly cap, and the count resets.

decisions.title: Wage
decisions.decides: The base wage, adjusted each month

rule.label: Productivity trend plus a response to slack
rule.text: Wage step = trend + wage_k x (reference unemployment - unemployment), capped each month, where the trend is the expected inflation plus the sector's productivity growth. The wage never falls below the legal minimum.

decisions.title: Price
decisions.decides: The price it charges, adjusted each month

rule.label: Move toward unit cost plus a markup
rule.text: Price moves a share (price adjust) of the way toward (1 + markup) x unit cost each month, never below the minimum price. Demand never enters: excess demand shows up in hiring, not in the price.

decisions.title: Green technology
decisions.decides: Whether to buy a step of clean technology this month, and whether to save for one

rule.label: Buy when the carbon bill over the payback period beats the cost
rule.text: A step is worthwhile when the carbon bill over the payback period is larger than its cost, or an emissions cap binds, and the firm is below the technology ceiling. The firm buys it if its cash above the reserve covers its share after any subsidy; otherwise it holds cash back for it.

decisions.title: Investment and borrowing
decisions.decides: How much capital to buy next month and how much to borrow for it

rule.label: Replace capital and grow toward expected sales, if the return beats the loan rate
rule.text: Planned capital = depreciation + accelerator x (capital that expected sales call for - capital), scaled by a gate that is high when the smoothed return beats the loan rate plus the hurdle, and capped. It pays part from free cash and asks the bank for the rest. A firm in distress plans nothing.

decisions.title: Dividends
decisions.decides: How much to pay its owners

rule.label: Pay a share of profit, never below the cash reserve
rule.text: Regular dividend = payout ratio x profit, but only out of cash above the reserve for payroll and debt service. Idle cash well above that is also paid out at a set rate.

decisions.title: Closing down
decisions.decides: Whether to default and close

rule.label: Default after months of missed payments
rule.text: Each month the firm misses interest, principal or wages it counts one more month in distress; a clean month resets the count. After enough months in a row, if it still owes money, it defaults and closes.

decisions.title: Founding a firm
decisions.decides: Whether to found a firm in the dormant slot

rule.label: A chance that grows with the return over the cost of borrowing
rule.text: Which household can found (a Worker or Manager with enough savings) and which slot are matched first. The chance this month = mobility rate x (sector return - cost of borrowing), between 0 and 1; the firm is founded if the month's random draw falls below it.

decisions.title: Spending
decisions.decides: How much to spend on food, goods and services this month

rule.label: Food first, then a share of what is left
rule.text: Food need = people x food per person; the household buys that first, up to its savings. Of what is left of last month's disposable income it spends its class's propensity; the owner classes also spend a small slice of net wealth. The total cannot exceed savings, and is split into goods and services.

decisions.title: Shopping
decisions.decides: Which firm in each market gets the money

rule.label: Cheaper firms with more stock get more
rule.text: Each firm's weight = its stock x (average price / its price) ^ elasticity. The budget is shared in proportion to weight, in two passes so a firm cannot sell more than it holds. What buyers wanted at their share, even beyond stock, is its demand. Firms buying capital goods and the government use the same split.

decisions.title: Expecting sales
decisions.decides: What sales to expect next month

rule.label: A smoothing of demand
rule.text: Expected sales = weight x this month's demand + (1 - weight) x last expectation. Hiring and production read it, so spending reaches jobs here.

decisions.title: Lobbying
decisions.decides: How much a capital-owning household gives to lobbying

rule.label: A share of capital income, within savings and the cap
rule.text: Spend = capital income x the smaller of the spend rate and the campaign cap, never more than savings. Which households lobby (Capitalists and Rentiers) and who receives the money are matched first.

decisions.title: Lending room
decisions.decides: How much more the bank may lend

rule.label: Equity divided by the required ratio
rule.text: Most the bank may have lent = equity / required capital ratio (nothing if the ratio is zero). Room = that less its loans, never below zero.

decisions.title: Lending
decisions.decides: How much to lend each firm that asks

rule.label: The request, within the bank's room and the firm's leverage cap
rule.text: Approved = the smallest of the request, the bank's remaining room, and (maximum leverage x firm assets - its debt), never below zero. Firms are served in order until the room is used up.

decisions.title: Interest rate
decisions.decides: The interest rate each firm pays

rule.label: Base rate plus a spread that grows with leverage
rule.text: Rate = policy rate + base spread + leverage spread x (debt / assets) + any extra spread the economic system adds. Riskier, more indebted firms pay more.

decisions.title: Bank payout
decisions.decides: How much of its excess capital the bank pays out

rule.label: Pay out part of equity above a buffer
rule.text: Required = loans x capital ratio x (1 + buffer). Excess = equity - required (never below zero). It pays out the payout share of the excess to its owner.

decisions.title: Rescue or failure
decisions.decides: What happens when the bank's equity goes negative

rule.label: The treasury recapitalises it, or depositors take a loss
rule.text: If equity is negative and the bailout policy is on, new money restores equity to the target share of loans. Without it the bank fails and every deposit loses a share: the shortfall over deposits, plus a margin.

decisions.title: Funding the month
decisions.decides: How to fund the month's payments: borrow the gap, or repay debt

rule.label: Cash and taxes first, then the bank, within its lending room
rule.text: The treasury needs this month's committed payments plus next month's planned purchases. If cash and taxes fall short, it borrows the gap, up to the bank's lending room. If they cover it, it repays a share of the surplus, up to what it owes.

decisions.title: Cutting spending
decisions.decides: How much of its payments to cut when the treasury runs short

rule.label: Every payment is cut by the same share
rule.text: If cash, taxes and borrowing cannot cover the committed payments, each payment is paid at the same share (funds over commitments) and the shortfall is reported. Otherwise everything is paid in full.

decisions.title: Legitimacy
decisions.decides: How its legitimacy moves each month

rule.label: Drifts with wellbeing, unemployment, inequality, debt, bailouts and system change
rule.text: Legitimacy changes by a wellbeing weight x (wellbeing - neutral), less a weight x the amount unemployment and the Gini exceed their thresholds, less a weight x the amount public debt exceeds a year's GDP, less a penalty if the bank was bailed out, less the resistance to a system change under way. It stays between 0 and 1.

decisions.title: Keeping the pilot
decisions.decides: Whether to let the pilot go, or hire the pilot back

rule.label: Let go after months of short pay, hired back once savings cover wages
rule.text: If the pilot is employed and has gone unpaid in full for the maximum number of months in a row, the pilot is let go. If not employed, with no other job, and the estate's savings cover the set months of wages, the pilot is hired back.

decisions.title: Flying the jet
decisions.decides: Whether the jet flies this month

rule.label: A monthly chance, and only with a pilot
rule.text: The simulation takes one random draw each month. The jet flies if the draw falls below the monthly chance and a pilot is on the payroll (or the town has no pilot).

decisions.title: Fencing off the commons
decisions.decides: Whether an owner fences off an open commons this month

rule.label: A monthly chance while the commons are open
rule.text: While the commons are open, each month's random draw is compared with the economic system's chance of enclosure; below it, the richest capital-owning household fences the commons off. Who that is, is matched in the simulation.
